//: The Wanderer from 3D (docs/ART.md '3D to sprites'). Render: blender -b art/3d/wanderer.blend --python tools/blender/render_layers.py -- art/3d/wanderer.json, then python3 tools/sprites_from_renders.py art/3d/wanderer.json --aseprite
//model: The game's name for this character (Appearance.Model, an outfit's "model"): its sheets are creatures/<model>, _skin, _eyes, _face, _hair and apparel/<item>_<model>, apart from the generated people's.
//pose: VRoid figures are ~7 heads tall in a T-pose: a bigger head toward the game's ~3, and arms down until there's an Idle action. The Wanderer's proportions are set in VRoid now, so bone_scale is empty.
//layers: Bottom to top, in the game's drawing order (Rendering/HumanLook.Layers). Roles: skin/hair/eyes/dye are tinted by the game (model them white or light grey); plain is drawn as is; base takes the outlines.
//materials: For tools/blender/setup_vrm.py: [part of a VRoid material name, collection], first match wins. Eye whites, lashes and brows are the untinted face detail; the iris is the tinted eyes layer.
//tints: Only for the hidden reference layer of the .aseprite: what the game multiplies each tinted sheet by for this preset.
//animations: For tools/blender/retarget_mixamo.py: action name -> Mixamo FBX (Without Skin, 30 fps; the walk In Place), relative to this file.
//tags: Every animation the game asks a person for. '{view}' expands to each view; 'frames' are Blender frame numbers sampled from the action; 'event' marks a frame of the tag (the hammer strike). Sleep and downed are seen from above, once.
